questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
I have several important aspects when I choose my study destination:
- The academic courses
- The city and the country; especially the nature 
- A country not too far away from Denmark - but still with a new culture and a lot of possibilities.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Overall a very nice experience - I would really recommend Iceland and Reykjavik University.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer:
Reykjavík University send a lots of useful information upon arrival. Furthermore, you could send them an e-mail with additional questions. 

Iceland is a very loose society with the motto 'þetta reddast' - so be aware that some information might show up last minute and exam dates etc can change during the exchange!

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: When I arrived at Reykjavik University, we had orientation days with a mixture of social and informal stuff. Furthermore it was always possible to reach out to the international team from the beginning to the end of the semester.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: The international team is very friendly and helpful!

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
It was difficult to find something to live in off campus - which resulted in a very expensive housing for a lot of us exchange students. 

Recommendation:
If you want to live off campus - use Facebook-groups recommended by the university to find housing.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer:
Pros of living off campus:
- Reykjavík University and the student housing closeby is located approximately 4 kilometres away from city centre Reykjavik. By living off campus you can choose housing based on your own preferences, such as being close to the city centre, to nature, to shopping center, to university etc.
- If you are lucky, the housing can be cheaper than the student housing at Reykjavík University.  
  
Cons of living off campus: 
- For me it was more expensive than living on campus
- Furthermore it was far away from the university.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
Tip: 
Apply for student housing and cheap off campus accommodation as fast as possible!

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was very easy to apply, and the answer time was quick as well.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The application/registration was through Mobility Online which is similar to the exchange application through UCPH.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The guides sent from the university was very helpful for me and made the proces easy. Furthermore it was possible to send them an e-mail with additional questions.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I did not get one of the classes I wanted, since the law department at Reykjavik University is quite small and not enough people applied for the course.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Remember that the law department at Reykjavik University is quite small, and do not offer a lot of courses. As mentioned above there is a chance that not enough people apply for the course resulting in a cancellation. With that said, they are flexible with running courses etc. even with few students.

Be aware that the Icelandic mindset and motto is 'þetta reddast' which means that sometimes you receive last minute information or dates of exams etc might change during the semester from the dates they told you in the beginning of the semester.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: One of my courses got cancelled - but they informed me and offered me other courses.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: In my opinion the overall level of the courses were a bit easier compared to UCPH - the reason therefore might be the fact that the courses were either 7.5 or 3.75 ECTS.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
Overall the teaching style was similar to UCPH; we had lectures in classrooms with a teacher presentation and some plenum discussions as well.

The most different thing from UCPH was the continious exams and grades. During the semester we had assignments and exams that was a part of the final grading. Furthermore in some courses you get a participation grade.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
US Litigation
The US Legal System: Sources and Structure
European Convention on Human Rights
International Criminal Law
Climate Law

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I really liked the courses:
US Litigation
The US Legal System: Sources and Structure

It was interesting to obtain a general knowledge about the legal system in the US, and the teacher was very good as well.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: In general a lot of things were more expensive than calculated - but the thing that surprised me the most was the expensive student housing/accommodation. The costs hereof was more expensive than stated at the calculated costs at the webpage of Reykjavik University.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
More expensive than expected: A lot of groceries, such as meat, vegetables etc. and as mentioned before accommodation

Less expensive than expected: Sweets and candy

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Reykjavík University did not offer a lot of sports opportunities. All departments had an association with activities such as visiting companies, parties etc. There was a cost of being a part of the association. Most of it was only offered in Icelandic - but besides that it was nice to participate in.  

Some exchange students did on their own plan soccer, bouldering etc.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
If you are in Iceland please do yourself the favor and enjoy the beautiful Icelandic nature.  

Everyone in Iceland will give you this tip: visit the local swimmingpools - that is a very social thing to do in Iceland!

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Experience the lovely and beautiful country of Iceland as much as you can. Even visiting the same places several times during the different seasons is nice!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: In general easy! Sometimes the information is given in Icelandic - but google translate helps a lot!

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: At the law department it was a bit difficult to socialize with the local students - if that is the case, then go to social events arranged by other (local) students, such as Erasmus networks, international committees etc.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer:
I did not really find it culturally challenging - since Iceland and Denmark is not too far away from each other. 

The Icelandic mindset is a bit more chill than the danish - they have the 'þetta reddast' motto, which translates to 'everything will work out'.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer:
I really enjoyed the more chill 'þetta reddast' mindset.

Furthermore the Icelandic people is very friendly and helpful!

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Three most important things:
- Apply for accommodation as fast as possible
- It is nice to participate in social events - it makes the academic part more fun as well 
- Enjoy the nature and Iceland as much as possible

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Everything is expensive - but do yourself the favor and experience as much as possible during weekends ect.

Rent a car with some of your new friends and enjoy waterfalls, glaciers, lava tunnels, puffins (when it is puffin-season) etc.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer:
- I improved my legal academic English skills
- I challenged myself 
- I really enjoyed slowing a bit down and enjoying the Icelandic nature 
- Furthermore I got a lot of good friends

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer:
For me the greatest challenge was to live in another country with other cultures etc. 

Furthermore it was a challenge to balance social and academic life.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Overall, I would really recommend Reykjavík University and Iceland!

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
